about.title: About Iskra
about.webTagline: A Matrix messenger in the browser — the same Iskra, without installing anything.
aboutMatrix.email.body: Your account lives on one server, and you can write to people on any other. Email works the same way: you’re on Gmail, your friend is on Yahoo, and the mail still arrives. A Matrix address looks like this: @name:server.
aboutMatrix.email.title: Like email, but for chats
aboutMatrix.intro: Matrix is an open way for messaging apps to talk to each other. Iskra is one of those apps. There are others, and they all understand each other.
aboutMatrix.nobody.body: Matrix isn’t owned by one company that could shut it down, sell your data or change the rules. There are thousands of servers, run by foundations, communities and ordinary people. You can run one too.
aboutMatrix.nobody.title: Nobody’s in charge
aboutMatrix.private.body: Messages are encrypted right on your device, and only the person you’re writing to can decrypt them. The server stores and passes them along, but it can’t read them.
aboutMatrix.private.title: Your conversations stay yours
aboutMatrix.title: What is Matrix
account.editOffline: Your profile can’t be changed offline — there’s no server to tell.
account.nameChangeNotice: Everyone you chat with will hear about a new name — a note appears in every chat you share.

appearance.previewAnswer: This one. What do you think?
appearance.wallpaperFooter: The wallpaper is the same in every conversation. Your photo stays on this device and is never sent anywhere.
beta.intro: The unfinished things live here. Turn one off if it gets in the way and back on if you change your mind: nothing breaks and nothing is lost.
beta.title: Beta features
beta.showsSourceHelp: A message’s menu gets “View JSON” — the event as the server sent it. Useful when a message shows up wrong.
beta.homeserverHelp: The address the app really talks to — found from the account’s name, not necessarily what was typed at sign-in. A bridge doesn’t change it; it only carries the connection.
beta.showsAllEventsHelp: Chats also show the events the app normally leaves out — permissions, join rules, calls, picture changes, anything that failed to parse — as a grey line with the type and the sender.

chats.enterSendsHelpWeb: Enter sends, Shift + Enter starts a new line.

chats.serviceHelp: The grey lines about who changed their name and who joined, left or was invited. A new chat name or photo is always shown.
chats.threadsHelpWeb: Replies in threads are gathered under their message as “3 replies”. Unless replies are hidden, they also appear in the chat itself, among the other messages. Personal chats have no threads.

elsewhere.linkPassed: The link has opened in that window — switch to it.

encryption.keyNeededHelp: Your old messages are encrypted, and this device can’t open them yet. Enter the code you saved when you turned the backup on.
encryption.newKeyHelp: The old code will stop working. Worth doing if it ended up somewhere it shouldn’t have.
encryption.offHelp: If you lose this device, nobody will be able to read your old messages — including you. Protect them, and we’ll give you the code that brings them back.
encryption.onHelp: Your conversations are kept on the server in a backup, encrypted. With your recovery code you can read them on any new device.
encryption.saveKeyHelp: We show it once and never again. Write it down or put it in a password manager: without it, your old messages don’t come back.

folders.emptyMessage: Chats that fit its rules will appear here.
folders.explanation: Folders gather chats by rules — personal, groups, unread — and sit as tabs above the list. They’re the same on all your devices.
folders.membershipFooter: Ticked, the chat is in the folder even if it doesn’t fit the rules. Unticked, it never is.
folders.saveFailed: The folders couldn’t be saved. Try again.

message.menu.deleteConfirmMessage: It’ll disappear for everyone in the chat, and it can’t be brought back.

reactions.quickHelp: Double-tap a message to leave it.
recording.hint: Tap to choose voice or video. Hold to record, and swipe up to keep recording hands-free.
recording.hintPointer: Click to record hands-free; right-click to choose voice or video. Hold to record, and move up to keep recording hands-free.
recovery.approve.message: The reset has to be approved on your server’s page. If you did that, carry on — and your old messages are gone for good. If you changed your mind, nothing happens.
recovery.approve.title: Did you approve it?
recovery.choose.message: Your earlier messages are encrypted, and this device can’t open them yet. There are two ways — both of them work.
recovery.choose.title: Unlock your messages
recovery.creating.message: We’re putting your messages into a backup so you can read them from any device. This can take a minute.
recovery.creating.title: Setting up your backup
recovery.enter.message: The code we showed you when the backup was turned on.
recovery.enter.title: Enter your recovery code
recovery.lost.alone.message: Without the code and without another device, your old messages can’t come back — they stay encrypted for good. New messages will arrive as usual, and we’ll give you a new recovery code.
recovery.lost.alone.notPassword: Your account password has nothing to do with this: it opens your account, not your old messages.
recovery.lost.alone.title: Let’s start fresh
recovery.lost.hasDevices: That’s all right. Confirm this device from a phone or computer where you’re already signed in, and we’ll give you a new code to replace the lost one.
recovery.lost.noAccess: I can’t get to that device
recovery.lost.title: Can’t find it?
recovery.new.keepOld: Later — I’ll go and look for the old one
recovery.new.message: The old code stops working immediately, and there is no getting it back. If you have it written down somewhere, that copy becomes useless.
recovery.new.title: Create a new code?
recovery.password.message: Your server is asking you to confirm it’s really you.
recovery.password.title: Enter your password
recovery.preparing: One moment, looking through your messages
recovery.save.confirm: I’ve written the code down somewhere safe
recovery.save.warning: If this code is lost and you have no other device, nobody can bring your old messages back — not us, not the server. They stay encrypted for good.
room.access.addressFooter: The address is how the chat is found and opened from a link. Clear it and the chat has none.
room.access.bannedFooter: They can’t come into the chat, even if invited.
room.access.historyFooter: What someone who joins later will see of what was already said. In a protected chat older messages may not open for them: they don’t have the keys.
room.access.inDirectoryHelp: People will find the chat when they search public rooms on {server}.
room.access.unbanHelp: They’ll be able to come in again. They won’t appear in the chat by themselves — invite them or send a link.
room.emptyMessage: Send the first message — that’s how it starts.
room.identity.changedBody: Messages to this person are now encrypted with new keys. That usually happens after signing in on a new phone. If you weren’t expecting it, check with them in person.
room.identity.failed: That didn’t work. Check your connection and try again.
room.identity.violationBody: You verified this person, but the keys have changed since. Until you’re sure it’s still them, don’t write anything important.
room.identity.violationTitle: {name}: keys no longer match the ones you verified
room.loadFailedMessage: The messages haven’t gone anywhere — we just couldn’t load them. Check your connection.
room.localName.help: Only you see this name, and only on this device. The other person is never told, your other devices keep the name they already had, and signing out forgets it.
room.manage.blockHelp: They will leave the chat and cannot come back until you unblock them.

room.manage.offline: With no network you can read this chat and write to it, but not change it.

roomList.emptyMessage: When someone messages you, it’ll show up here.

roomList.new.searchFailed: The server didn’t answer the search
roomList.peek.staysUnread: Just peeking — nothing gets marked as read

servers.intro: Your account lives on one server, and you can write to people on any other — just like email. On every server below you can create an account right in Iskra.
servers.matrixOrg: The largest Matrix server, run by the foundation that develops Matrix itself.
servers.nopeChat: Run by the adminForge team, who host other free services too. Has bridges to other messengers.
servers.ownAbout: You can run a server of your own — then your conversations are entirely in your hands. You’ll need a domain and a little time.
servers.quassel: An open server for everyday conversation, free for everyone.
servers.tchncs: One of the oldest community servers. Its owner runs other free services too.
servers.title: Choose a server

session.ended.title: You are no longer signed in
session.offlineMessage: Your conversations are here, on this device. We just can’t reach the server right now — check your network.

storage.cache.explained: Downloads. They come back when needed.
storage.cacheWeb: The conversation cache on this device. It downloads again when needed; encryption keys and your sign-in stay.
storage.confirm.body: The app will reload. Messages, photos and files will download again when you open them, and for a while search will not find everything. You stay signed in.
storage.confirm.title: Clear the cache?
storage.dock.message: Safari erases data for sites you haven’t opened in a week — encryption keys included. It leaves apps in the Dock alone: File → Add to Dock.
storage.dock.title: Add Iskra to the Dock so Safari doesn’t erase it

storage.notPersisted: The browser may erase Iskra’s data if space runs low — including keys that exist nowhere else.
storage.persist: Ask the browser to keep it
storage.persist.message: When your disk runs low, Firefox may erase Iskra’s data — encryption keys included. It’s about to ask whether Iskra can keep them safely.
storage.persist.title: Keep your conversations safe?
storage.persisted: The browser has promised not to erase Iskra’s data, even if space runs low.
storage.search.confirm.body: The app will reload. For a while search will not find everything — the index fills again as you read. Your messages and photos stay where they are.
